summary.intent: Implement work package N in the callisto repo: change the `cascade.peer-escalation` default to false so peer-dependent bumps get a patch (matching Changesets v3), and also update PR bodies for #562 and #564 with observed flakes.
summary.outcome: Pushed PR #568 on branch feat/peer-default-patch (linked to trail #458) with the default flipped, docs, changeset, and tests updated. The #562 and #564 PR bodies were updated. Lint, pre-push, doc-check and doctests pass; full test run has 1 failure, a registry test that was not confirmed as the known flake.

repo: The peer-escalation default is resolved in crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs and documented in docs/config.md; cascade scenario tests live in crates/callisto-cli/tests/cascade_scenarios_tests.rs.
Changesets are created with `cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add --package cargo/<name>:<level> --summary ...`; breaking changes get a `**Breaking:**` paragraph in the summary.
Gate commands are `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test` (nextest) and `cargo test --doc --workspace`; `just test` exits 100 on any failing test.

Flipping the default broke two existing tests that relied on major escalation: promoted_dual_dependent_preserves_aliases_across_cascade_and_release_floor and release_decision_names_the_dual_source_distribution_each_dependent_uses. A test fixture also needed edge kind "Peer" capitalized in version_tests.rs.

The test `callisto-graph registry::tests::a_version_the_registry_serves_is_exact_with_no_checksum_or_yank_claim` runs the real `cargo info` and intermittently fails with CommandFailed; it is believed (not confirmed) to be the fixture-portability flake that #560 addresses.
Branches are linked to trails with `entire trail link <n>`, and `entire trail ci-pr` shows which PR backs a trail. PR bodies carry an `<!-- entire-shadow-pr -->` marker.
Builds are run with CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0, CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 to limit resource use; `rm -rf target` is run afterwards in the worktree.

code.finding: The peer_escalation default and its resolve test were edited here to default to false.
The promoted dual dependent assertion was simplified to always expect Severity::Patch, since the co_release branch no longer yields Major.
The peer-app fixture edge kind changed from "peer" to "Peer" so it matches the edge kind casing the code expects.

workflow: Compound shell commands combining git switch/add/commit/push were split into separate plain commands after the combined call failed to run.
Verifying commit signatures via `gh api .../commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` is part of the PR routine.
Temp files were moved from $TMPDIR to a job-specific tmp directory when the variable was unreliable in the shell.

friction: `just test` repeatedly failed, with failures varying between runs, making it hard to tell regressions from flakes.
A flaky registry test (real `cargo info`) failed with CommandFailed on several full-workspace runs but passed in isolation; its cause was not found.
`just test` once reported `commands::init::tests::an_existing_config_errors` as leaky, with an unknown cause.
`just pre-push` initially failed on formatting only, requiring `cargo fmt`.
The first combined git command chain did not run as written and had to be split into individual commands.
The command for locating the plan file and worktree path needed several attempts because of path differences between the main repo and the worktree.
open_items: PRs #560, #562, #564 and #568 are not yet merged.
The remaining failing registry test is assumed, not confirmed, to be the flake fixed by #560; verify once #560 lands.
The cause of the intermittent `just test` failures (exit 100) and the leaky init test is still unexplained.
`just ci`, `just bench` and mutants were not run for WP N.
WP K is not started, as it waits on Session 1 merging G; it goes on trail #458.
